# SlideQueue

The slots a presentation's slides are staged into, and which one is on screen.

## Anatomy

A header with the queue's name and a summary, then one row per slot: its number, its title, and a clear action when it is filled.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `slots` *(required)* | `QueueSlot[]` | — | — |
| `label` *(required)* | `string` | — | Names the list — "Slide queue". |
| `summary` | `string` | `''` | The mono note on the right of the header — "4 of 8 filled". |
| `openLabel` *(required)* | `string` | — | — |
| `clearLabel` *(required)* | `string` | — | — |
| `emptyLabel` *(required)* | `string` | — | — |
| `onopen` | `(slot: QueueSlot) => void` | — | — |
| `onclear` | `(slot: QueueSlot) => void` | — | — |

## Variants

Empty, filled and loaded per slot.

## States

Empty slot, filled slot, loaded slot.

## Keyboard

| Key | Behaviour |
| --- | --- |
| `Tab` | Moves through each slot's open action, then its clear action. |
| `Enter`, `Space` | Opens or clears. |

## ARIA

A named region containing a real list. Each action's accessible name carries the slot number and title, so "clear" is never announced without saying what is being cleared.

## Accessibility acceptance criteria

- Reachable, operable and leavable by keyboard alone, with a focus indicator meeting 3:1 in both schemes.
- An accessible name for every control, and current state exposed programmatically.
- No meaning carried by colour alone.
- Legible and operable at a 360px viewport and at desktop width, and at 200% zoom.
- Interactive targets at least 44 × 44px on touch-capable viewports.

## Recorded deviations

| What | Why |
| --- | --- |
| `--ui-target-min` | The reference makes the clear control 38px wide, below the 44px minimum this system holds every touch target to. |
| The loaded state carries a word as well as a colour. | The reference distinguishes empty, filled and loaded by border style and fill colour alone. |
| Action names include the slot. | The reference's clear control is a bare `×` with no name. |
